sec: Type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome and BMI

items.q: Match the natural-history stage to its position in the diagram — 1) Early stage 2) Middle stage 3) Transitional glucose stage 4) Late stage … A) Genetics/environment B) Obesity C) IFG/IGT D) Late diabetes
items.exp: The natural-history diagram proceeds through genetics/environment, obesity, dyslipidemia/hypertension and IFG/IGT before early and late diabetes. (Book p922)

items.q: The line labelled above the natural-history diagram that falls with advancing age is:
items.exp: The vertical axis of the natural-history figure is beta-cell function, which declines across advancing age. (Book p922)

items.q: Assess the natural-history diagram: I Hyperinsulinemia appears before hyperglycemia. II Macrovascular complications are shown before microvascular complications.
items.exp: The diagram places hyperinsulinemia before hyperglycemia and labels macrovascular complications earlier than microvascular complications. (Book p922)

items.q: Apart from dyslipidemia and hypertension, which group is explicitly listed as other Type 2 DM comorbidities?
opts: NAFL, hypogonadism, periodontal disease, fracture and atherosclerosis
Asthma, migraine, cataract, gout and otitis
Pneumonia, nephritis, anemia, fever and rash
Hepatitis, cirrhosis, jaundice, ascites and pruritus
items.exp: The right-hand list gives NAFL, hypogonadism, periodontal disease, fracture and atherosclerosis. (Book p922)

items.q: How many of the five metabolic-syndrome criteria should be met according to the page?
items.exp: The metabolic-syndrome heading states that any 3 of 5 should be met. (Book p922)

items.q: Match the metabolic-syndrome criterion to the printed cut-off — 1) Male waist circumference 2) Female waist circumference 3) Triglycerides 4) Male HDL … A) >102 cm B) >88 cm C) >150 mg/dL D) <40 mg/dL
items.exp: The criteria list male waist >102 cm, female waist >88 cm, triglycerides >150 mg/dL and male HDL <40 mg/dL. (Book p922)

items.q: The fifth metabolic-syndrome criterion on the page is impaired fasting glucose above ___ mg/dL.
items.exp: The fifth criterion is impaired fasting glucose (IFG) >100 mg/dL. (Book p922)

items.q: Assess the HDL and blood-pressure entries: I Female HDL is listed as less than 50 mg/dL. II Blood pressure is listed as greater than 130/85.
items.exp: The metabolic-syndrome list gives female HDL <50 mg/dL and BP >130/85. (Book p922)

items.q: What Indian BMI value is used for the obese category in the table?
items.exp: The Indian-criteria column labels obese as >25. (Book p922)

items.q: Match the BMI category with the Indian criteria — 1) Normal 2) Overweight 3) Obese … A) 18–22.9 B) 23–24.9 C) >25
items.exp: The table gives Indian BMI normal 18–22.9, overweight 23–24.9 and obese >25. (Book p922)

items.q: Which set matches the page's Indian-population diabesity/adiposopathy list?
opts: Waist >90 cm in men or >80 cm in women, hyperglycemia, HTN, hyperlipidemia with increased CRP/decreased adiponectin, and a prothrombotic state
Waist >102 cm in men only with hypoglycemia and low CRP
BMI below 18 with bradycardia and reduced clotting
HDL above 50 with isolated post-load glucose rise
items.exp: The diabesity/adiposopathy list uses male waist >90 cm, female waist >80 cm, hyperglycemia, HTN, hyperlipidemia with increased CRP/decreased adiponectin, and a prothrombotic state. (Book p922)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the five items in the Indian-population diabesity list?
items.exp: Hypercalcemia is not in the printed diabesity/adiposopathy list; hyperglycemia, HTN and prothrombotic state are listed. (Book p922)
